questions.prompt: Fictional GDP release: consensus +0.4% on the quarter, actual +0.1%. What is the surprise?

options.explanation: No: surprise is actual minus consensus, and the actual is lower.
No: that is the actual figure, not the gap.

questions.prompt: In most countries, who sets the policy interest rate?

options.explanation: No: the government sets taxes and spending, which is fiscal policy.
Right: the policy rate is the central bank's main monetary-policy tool.
No: statistics offices publish data such as GDP and inflation; they do not set rates.

questions.prompt: Hypothetical: government debt 300 billion WMK, yearly GDP 600 billion WMK. What is debt as a share of GDP?

options.explanation: No: that divides GDP by debt. Divide debt by GDP.
No: that is the debt in billions, read as a percentage.

questions.prompt: Suppose traders' bets imply a 90% chance of a 0.25-point rate rise. The fictional central bank holds rates instead. Measured against what was priced in, what is the surprise?

options.text: 0 points, as rates did not move
options.explanation: No: the market expected a rise, so no change is itself a surprise.
No: that assumes the rise was certain. It was priced at 90%.

questions.prompt: The price of fictional Westmark's main export falls 15%. What is most accurate about WMK?

options.text: WMK must fall 15% too, matching its export
options.explanation: No: there is no one-to-one link, and other forces can outweigh it.

options.text: It tends to weigh on WMK; other forces also matter
options.explanation: Right: lower export earnings can reduce demand for WMK, as a tendency, not a rule.

options.text: Buyers abroad now need less WMK, which may push it up
options.explanation: No: needing less WMK means less demand for it, which tends to weigh on it, not lift it.

questions.prompt: Two fictional inflation releases show the same consensus and actual. After one, the currency rises and holds; after the other, it spikes and falls back. What best explains the difference?

options.text: One release must have been reported wrongly
options.explanation: No: both numbers can be correct. The setup before them differed.

options.text: One release may have had a bigger surprise than the other
options.explanation: No: the same consensus and actual means the same surprise. The setup before them differed.

options.text: More was priced in before the second, so traders took profit
options.explanation: Right: when many traders bought early, good news can be when they take profit.
